transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Time: 1:00 PM ET
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Raj (CSM), Marco (SE), Dr. Emily (CTO), James (Head of Data), Priya (Security), Lena (PM)

[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Good to meet you all, I'm Sophie, AE at Redwood. Quick agenda
[00:12] Dr. Emily: Yep, that's great. Thanks Sophie. We're excited to get started; we want to use Redwood for clinical note summarization and patient triage routing. Main concerns are PHI handling and latency for triage.
[00:30] James: Yeah hi, James here. We run on a hybrid infra, some data in our cloud, some on-prem EHR. We'll probably start with de-identified extracts but need options for private deployment.
[00:45] Marco: Got it. Quick follow, when you say triage latency what are you targeting? 200 ms, 500 ms?
[00:50] James: Ideally sub-500ms p95 for short prompts; for long summarization maybe 1.5s p95 is ok. But cost matters — we can't burn a ton for every request.
[01:05] Raj: That's helpful. For pilot we usually recommend a small dedicated pool or hosted with a quantized model to control cost — we can recommend config after we see traffic.
[01:20] Priya: From security, we need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration for key management, audit logs, and the ability to turn off third-party telemetry. Also data residency — some records must remain in our US region, and some customers in CA require additional controls.
[01:40] Sophie: Absolutely. We'll send our security pack with SOC2 attestations, our DPA template, and details on KMS/HSM integrations. For private deployments we support VPC connectors and on-prem packages; Marco can speak to the technical setup.
[02:00] Marco: Right — at a high level: for VPC we can do VPC peering or private link; we support customer-managed KMS. There's also an on-prem bundle but that needs planning for resource sizing and network egress. For the pilot, many customers start with hosted API with strict retention rules and then move to Dedicated or Private if they need isolation.
[02:28] Lena: What's the approximate timeline for moving to a private instance once we decide?
[02:33] Marco: Depends — typically 4-8 weeks for Private with sizing and security review, less for Dedicated. Hosted is immediate once accounts are provisioned.
[02:46] Dr. Emily: That's doable. We want to run a two-week pilot: ingest 50k de-identified notes, run summarization + triage model, measure latency/cost/accuracy. If we hit p95 < 700ms and accuracy within 90% of baseline, we'll consider Dedicated.
[03:05] Sophie: Great — two-week pilot is a good plan. We'll help scope the dataset and provide test harnesses for benchmarking.
[03:15] James: One concern — our legal team will need to review the DPA and the logging policy. Who should I loop in?
[03:22] Sophie: Please loop in your legal contact and Priya can coordinate on the compliance items. I'll include our legal and security PDFs in the pack.
[03:30] Priya: Also please clarify data deletion policies and retention windows. We have some retention requirements of 90 days for test artifacts.
[03:38] Marco: We can set retention per-organization and per-route. By default hosted retention is short but we can configure longer retention for audit, or turn off logs for certain routes per policy.
[03:50] Dr. Emily: Good. For integration, we're leaning towards starting with Redwood's hosted API to move fast, then pivot if needed. We'll need SDKs and example code for Node and Python.
[04:05] Raj: We'll share quickstart templates and a sample repo. Also, we'll assign a CSM (that's me) to help with onboarding tasks and weekly check-ins.
[04:16] Sophie: On the technical side, Marco will run a deep-dive on networking — he'll need the names/emails of your infra and network folks.
[04:25] James: I'll add Mark (our infra lead) to the thread and send sample datasets.
[04:30] Marco: Perfect. Also, can you share expected concurrency (QPS) and average prompt length? That helps us recommend batching and model variant.
[04:40] James: For triage ~50 RPS during business hours peak, average prompt 80 tokens; summarization low QPS but large prompts ~800 tokens.
[04:55] Marco: So for triage we might recommend a smaller, faster model with aggressive quantization and batch size, while for summarization we can use a larger model with KV cache enabled. We'll run cost/latency estimates in the next call.
[05:10] Lena: About billing and cost — will we get itemized token-level breakdowns? We need cost attribution by route.
[05:17] Raj: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and per-route breakdowns, you can also map to internal cost centers. We'll demo that in the onboarding.
[05:28] Priya: One more item: audit logs. We need immutable logs for certain workflows for compliance. Is that supported?
[05:35] Marco: Yes, we can ship audit logs to your S3 or to a customer-managed log collector; immutable retention policies depend on storage. We'll detail options in the security pack.
[05:48] Dr. Emily: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood side to start pilot?
[05:53] Sophie: We just need contact points, sample dataset, and acceptance criteria. We'll provision sandbox keys and share quickstarts within 48 hours after docs are signed.
[06:05] James: Legal will likely take 1-2 weeks on the DPA. Can the pilot start with redacted data before DPA final?
[06:12] Priya: From our perspective, redacted data is fine for initial testing but for validation we'll need the DPA in place before production data is used.
[06:22] Sophie: That's standard. We'll proceed with de-identified data for the initial run.
[06:28] Marco: Planning note — we'll measure p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and token cost per route. I'll prepare a benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:35] Lena: Who will own the weekly check-ins?
[06:38] Raj: I'll run weekly onboarding syncs and escalate technical items to Marco.
[06:42] Sophie: Quick recap, action items and next steps — Sophie will send onboarding & security pack; Marco will schedule technical deep-dive; James to provide data and infra contacts; Priya to surface compliance constraints; Raj will set up weekly cadence.
[06:58] Dr. Emily: Thanks everyone. This seems like a good plan.
[07:02] Sophie: Great — we'll follow up with dates. Thanks all.

Notes on transcription: occasional overlaps and small mis-hearings, e.g., "KV cache" was sometimes transcribed as "K V cache" and product names like Redwood Dedicated came across as "Redwood dedicated pool" in the auto-transcript.
